description: Snowflake multi-pattern matching, live-verified: x LIKE ANY (p1, p2, ...) is TRUE when x matches at least ONE pattern, LIKE ALL when it matches EVERY pattern, and ILIKE ANY is the case-insensitive form. NULL patterns are SKIPPED rather than three-valued - 'a' LIKE ALL ('a', NULL) is TRUE and 'a' LIKE ANY ('b', NULL) is FALSE - and only a NULL SUBJECT or an ALL-NULL pattern list yields NULL. A numeric subject coerces to text. NOT LIKE ANY/ALL, ILIKE ALL and LIKE SOME do not exist in Snowflake and are rejected here too. An optional ESCAPE applies to EVERY pattern. Converted 1:1 from query/LikeAnyAllTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE words (w VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO words VALUES ('alpha'), ('beta'), ('gamma'), (NULL)
SELECT w FROM words WHERE w LIKE ANY ('al%', '%eta') ORDER BY w
CREATE TABLE words (w VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO words VALUES ('alpha'), ('beta'), ('gamma'), (NULL)
SELECT w FROM words WHERE w ILIKE ANY ('AL%', 'GA%') ORDER BY w
CREATE TABLE words (w VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO words VALUES ('alpha'), ('beta'), ('gamma'), (NULL)
SELECT w FROM words WHERE w LIKE ALL ('a%', '%a', '%lph%') ORDER BY w
CREATE TABLE words (w VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO words VALUES ('alpha'), ('beta'), ('gamma'), (NULL)
SELECT w FROM words WHERE w LIKE ANY ('bet_') ORDER BY w
SELECT NULL LIKE ANY ('a%', 'b%') AS r
SELECT 'a' LIKE ANY ('a', NULL) AS r
SELECT 'a' LIKE ANY ('b', NULL) AS r
SELECT 'a' LIKE ALL ('a', NULL) AS r
SELECT 'a' LIKE ALL ('b', NULL) AS r
SELECT 'a' LIKE ANY (NULL) AS r
SELECT 'a' LIKE ALL (NULL, NULL) AS r
SELECT 1 LIKE ANY ('1') AS r
SELECT 'a' NOT LIKE ANY ('a', 'b')
SELECT 'A' ILIKE ALL ('a%')
SELECT 'a' LIKE SOME ('a', 'b')
CREATE TABLE pct (v VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO pct VALUES ('50%'), ('50x')
SELECT v FROM pct WHERE v LIKE ANY ('50!%', '60!%') ESCAPE '!' ORDER BY v
SELECT 'axb' LIKE ANY ('a!_b') ESCAPE '!' AS r
SELECT 'a_b' LIKE ANY ('a!_b') ESCAPE '!' AS r

CREATE FUNCTION kind_of(w VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS
$$ SELECT CASE WHEN UPPER(w) ILIKE ANY ('AL%', 'BE%') THEN 'ab' ELSE 'other' END $$
SELECT kind_of('beta') AS r, kind_of('gamma') AS r2
